findings.title: Per-force timing — assigned to this slice by the plan — is deferred to slice 142
findings.description: The parent plan's entry for 141 explicitly scopes "per-tick timings broken down by phase (spatial build, spatial query, CSR assembly, **force totals per force**, integration)." The design makes `force_total` a single aggregate and pushes per-force resolution to slice 142. Slice 142's own plan entry only calls for implementing and benchmarking a cohesion `@ti.kernel` — it does not assign building per-force instrumentation. Dropping scope assigned to this slice leaves 142 to either build the instrumentation itself or benchmark without the resolution its design says it needs. Either keep per-force breakdown here (even as an optional field populated by the NumPy backend) or get the scope formally moved to 142.

findings.title: Workload schema example uses 3D coordinates while the engine is 2D
findings.description: The authoritative `mid-flock` YAML example uses `world_size: [200.0, 200.0, 200.0]` and 3-element `cluster_centers`, but the engine is 2D (`DIMS = 2` in `src/migratory/__init__.py`) and `AgentState` allocates `(n, DIMS)` arrays. The task breakdown for this same slice (T23–T25) already uses 2-element vectors (`[400.0, 400.0]`), confirming the design example is stale. Since workload YAML is the cross-slice contract future slices will copy, a schema example that cannot load against the engine is a real integration defect. Correct the example (and the schema prose) to 2D, or state the dimensionality rule explicitly.

findings.title: Integration-point descriptions reference engine symbols that do not exist
findings.description: The design claims profile names "resolve ... to the existing `BehavioralProfile` constructors used in `config/default.yaml`" and that "the harness does not invent new profiles." But `config/default.yaml` defines only one profile (`"default"`); there are no `flocker`/`leader` presets, so the harness necessarily invents them. Likewise, force names are said to "resolve to module-level singleton instances ... (e.g. `flocking.cohesion_force`)," yet the engine defines force *classes* (`CohesionForce`, etc.) with no such module-level singletons. These are hidden dependencies: the design points consumers at symbols that aren't there, while leaving the actual profile values and force wiring unspecified. State plainly that the bench owns a small local registry of concrete `BehavioralProfile`/`BulkForce` instances and record their values, so downstream slices have a real contract to rely on.

findings.title: Restated NFR value from slice 140 is wrong (50 µs vs 10 µs)
findings.description: The design cites slice 140's micro-benchmark as "`from_numpy_state` < 50 µs." Slice 140's actual Performance NFR and success criterion are **< 0.01 ms (10 µs)** at N=3,500 — a 5× tighter target. Misstating a prerequisite slice's performance contract in the design is misleading and could lead a future reader to accept a materially slower construction. Correct the figure to match slice 140.
